issues.failure_explanation: The proof introduces a quaternion q satisfying the sum-similarity equation, then redefines q as q1 q2 with q2 centralizing b1, but never shows that this new q is the sum-similarity quaternion or that such a factorization exists. The substitution into the sum-similarity equation is therefore unjustified, and the converse direction is not proved. The proof also ignores the boundary case where the sums are real, which lies outside the stated nonreal similarity lemma.

When Im(a) = -Im(b), the square root is an arbitrary pure quaternion and the condition Im(a) dot Im(q) = 0 is necessary. Without it, the displayed family contains non-solutions, for example a=i, b=-i, q=i.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem is stated for all nonreal pairwise-similar quaternions, but if Im(a1) x Im(a2)=0 (hence Im(b1) x Im(b2)=0), the square-root argument is zero and the auxiliary quaternions a3,b3 in the proof are real zero. The invoked quaternion-square-root lemma and homogeneous-Sylvester theorem require nonzero/nonreal inputs, so the formula and proof are ill-defined or outside their hypotheses in the collinear observation case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a nondegeneracy hypothesis Im(a1) x Im(a2) != 0, or provide a separate collinear case using the single-pair solution, since a2=t a1 and b2=t b1 makes the second alignment automatic once the first holds.
issues.overall_effect: The closed-form solution formula fails for parallel vector pairs; the claimed general solution set is not established in that regime.
issues.title: Main theorem formula undefined for collinear observations
issues.why_classification: This is a degenerate boundary case; a short local hypothesis or simple case split using the already-proven single-pair result restores the full scope without new architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed commutator equality drops the lambda2 square-root contribution to q2 b1 - b1 q2, implicitly assuming that square root commutes with b1. This is not proved and is false for arbitrary square roots when a3 b3^* is negative real, i.e. when a3=-b3. The stated condition, and the use of q1^* rather than q1^{-1} in the trigger, does not select the required branch. For example, with a1=i, a2=j, b1=i, b2=-j and q1=2, the formula admits q2=2j, giving q=4j, but the first alignment then yields -i instead of i. Hence the claimed general solution set contains non-solutions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the q2 prescription to require the square-root branch that commutes with b1 (equivalently, in the a3=-b3 case, Im(q2) parallel to b1), correct the scale-sensitive condition to use q1^{-1} or a scale-invariant condition, and prove the converse that all listed quaternions are solutions.
issues.overall_effect: The main closed-form theorem is false as stated because its parameterization can produce quaternions that do not make the Wahba cost zero.
issues.title: Main theorem admits extraneous square-root branches
issues.why_classification: The repair is local but requires a nontrivial branch-selection condition and proof; it corrects the main theorem without abandoning the central claim.
